diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitute lx=ly=0 and ux=uy=1 into the four exact Definition inequalities (lines 30–32): w>=0, w>=x+y-1, w<=x, w<=y. Only the illustration is specialized; ordered finite endpoint cases including zero widths remain in the unchanged Definition.

A=(0,0,0), B=(1,0,0), C=(0,1,0), D=(1,1,1) satisfy all four bounds. ABC has w=0; BCD has w=x+y-1; ACD has w=x; ABD has w=y. Each other vertex satisfies the corresponding half-space strictly. The local bilinear-hull lemma proof steps 1.2 and 2.3 give the same normalized vertices and coefficients W, X-W, Y-W, 1-X-Y+W, verifying that these four planes bound exactly the depicted tetrahedron.

For t in {1/4,1/2,3/4}, each fixed-y segment from (0,t,0) to (1,t,t) has w=tx=xy. Each fixed-x segment from (t,0,0) to (t,1,t) has w=ty=xy. The four slack values for graph points are xy, (1-x)(1-y), x(1-y), and (1-x)y, all nonnegative on [0,1]^2; this also matches the local hull lemma step 1.1.

The actual standalone native diagram crop displays all six dashed cyan edges AB, BC, CA, AD, DB, CD; each of four named vertices has degree three. Triangle ABC closes with the explicit C--A segment. The orange curves are six surface ruling segments, not additional polytope edges. The oblique 3D projection can cross traces without creating a new vertex; no crossing is asserted to be a junction.
The original item remains a definition and supplies no proof; the existing separate bilinear-hull lemma and all its proof steps are unchanged. No proof depends on the illustration.
